anya: Hey all — trying to get our SDK to run inside Next.js middleware (Edge). Import fails at startup with "Reference to node:crypto not allowed in Edge". Any lightweight pattern so we don't have to split into two npm packages?

matt: We solved this by adding an explicit edge subpath export and a tiny edge build. No need for separate repo.

rachel: Steps we used:
1) create src/edge-entry.ts that only imports pure runtime-safe code
2) build with esbuild: platform=browser, format=esm, target=es2020
3) add an exports subpath `./edge` pointing at dist/edge.mjs
Then middleware imports from `@pkg/edge`.

anya: Does that preserve TS types? I worry VSCode won't find types for the subpath.

matt: We ship `dist/edge.d.ts` and use `typesVersions` mapping so `@pkg/edge` resolves to that d.ts in TS. Example in package.json: `"typesVersions": {"*": {"./edge": ["dist/edge.d.ts"]}}`. Tsc picks it up.

rachel: Also watch transitive deps — a metrics client brought in `node:fs`. For the edge build we stubbed the metrics module with a tiny no-op shim that throws when invoked outside server context. That kept bundle tiny.

anya: Any pitfalls with bundlers/lockfiles? CI caught our first failure.

matt: Yes — monorepo/hoisted installs or pnpm sometimes resolve to the main entry. Use explicit `import { create } from '@pkg/edge'` in middleware. Also add a unit smoke test: `esbuild --bundle dist/edge.mjs --platform=browser` and run on miniflare or playwright to validate.

rachel: We added a lint rule preventing new public entry files from importing node builtins. Prevents regressions.

anya: Thanks — I'll try the subpath + edge build + typesVersions approach and post CI output if it still fails.
